why: The answer uses the wrong rule that a row can be all zeros. Every probability row must sum to 1. The answer also blames missing links, but outDegree is 5. The real cause is int division: counts[j] / outDegree is 0 for 0, 2 and 1 divided by 5.

concepts.why: Accepts a row that sums to 0 as a valid probability row, which is the RowsNeedNotSumToOne misconception.

concepts.quote: it just means the page has no links
concepts.why: Says a page with no links can have an all-zero row, when it needs 1/N in every column. Here the page is not even dangling, since outDegree is 5.
Makes no claim about the expression counts[j] / outDegree or its int type.
Does not mention the int division that cuts 2/5 and 1/5 down to 0.
